Chókwè was flooded on 17 January.headline: Flooding within 3 km of Chókwè: supported as of 17 Jan 2026, 03:42 UTC (NISAR Beta), 42% of the area newly under open water
reasons: claim refers to 17 Jan; NISAR looked on 17 Jan, 03:42 UTC
42% of the 3 km disk (1,191 ha) is newly under open water, 75% of its open ground
Copernicus agrees: the 16 Jan Sentinel-1 map calls 69% of its mapped part flooded, the 18 Jan COSMO-SkyMed map 51%
Only 2% of the new water was already dark on 5 Jan

Guijá ficou inundada no dia 17 de janeir.headline: No new open water detected within 3 km of Guijá: contradicted as of 17 Jan 2026, 03:42 UTC (NISAR Beta)
reasons: claim refers to 17 Jan; NISAR looked on 17 Jan, 03:42 UTC
0.3 ha of new open water in the 3 km disk (0.01%)
The dry rule applies here: 98% of the disk is open ground (it needs 50%), 98% is scored against Copernicus, only 2% is unclear (limit 10%), and there are no mapped buildings
Copernicus (Sentinel-1, 17 Jan, 03:18 UTC) maps none of it flooded
Flooding under crops, trees or between buildings does not show as open water
Compare Xai-Xai, where 12% of the disk is unclear (limit 10%), so the dry rule cannot fire there

Xai-Xai não alagou.headline: Flooding within 3 km of Xai-Xai: not provable as of 17 Jan 2026, 03:42 UTC (NISAR Beta), 6% of the area newly under open water
reasons: claim gives no date; NISAR looked on 17 Jan, 03:42 UTC
6% of the 3 km disk (181 ha) is newly under open water: too little to call it flooded, too much to call it dry
The dry rule cannot fire: 12% of the disk is unclear (radar brightness rose), above the 10% limit
26% of the disk is built-up, and flooding between buildings does not show as open water
Copernicus calls 1% of it flooded on 16 Jan (Sentinel-1) and 7% on 18 Jan (COSMO-SkyMed)

Macia was under water yesterday.headline: Flooding within 3 km of Macia: not provable as of 17 Jan 2026, 03:42 UTC (NISAR Beta), 0.04% of the area newly under open water
reasons: claim says "yesterday", which gives no fixed date; NISAR looked on 17 Jan, 03:42 UTC
Macia is on the NISAR grid but outside both Copernicus maps, so nothing independent checks it
NISAR saw neither enough new water (1 ha, 0.04% of the disk) nor clearly dry open ground: only 38% of the disk is open ground (the dry rule needs 50%), and 62% is built-up

Maputo flooded on 17 Jan.headline: Claim: not observable as of 17 Jan 2026, 03:42 UTC (no place matched inside the NISAR areas)
reasons: claim refers to 17 Jan; NISAR looked on 17 Jan, 03:42 UTC
No place in the claim matches the 50 places inside the three NISAR areas (Chókwè to Xai-Xai, Chinhangane, Palmeira)
